figures.caption: Figure 1: PC-ALM credit alignment in a scalar two-layer network (y = w2w1x; h = w1x; x=y=1). (A) BP loss landscape with BP and equilibrated-PC iso-loss curves. (B) Arrows are negative weight gradients for BP, equilibrated PC, and PC-ALM at different iterations. (C) Inference trace. PC settles h at heq; PC-ALM returns h to h0 = w1x while λ converges to the BP adjoint λ∞ = (y−w2h0)w2. Here, we take 10 primal steps before each dual step to emphasize the role of the dual as a lagged integrator of error; in Algorithm 1 we alternate between one primal and one dual step.
Figure 2: Width-depth results on Fashion-MNIST. PC-ALM matches BP at a budget of T = 2L across the full range of N , L, and activations. PC-ALM outperforms PC in deep narrow networks.

Figure 3: Diffusive versus ballistic credit propagation. ReLU residual MLP with N = 32, L = 64 on a Fashion-MNIST sample at initialization. The middle plot shows that the prediction error ri (left axis scale) leads the dual λi (right axis scale) across the network. PC-ALM enables faster and more even credit propagation across the network compared to PC.
Figure 4: Linear PC-ALM inference dynamics. (A) Eigenvalues of the block iteration matrix M . (B, C) Primal and dual neuron activity traces.

Figure 5: Cosine between the PC-ALM weight gradient and the BP weight gradient at an initialized network. (A) Alignment as a function of iteration, normalized to L. (B) Alignment as a function of iteration t, in units of c = t √ αηh/L across different depths and widths.

Figure 6: Parameterization sweep on Fashion-MNIST at fixed (N,L) = (32, 64), single seed, α = 1. Top row: λsp interpolates from standard parameterization (λsp=0) to mean field (λsp=1) at γ0=1. Bottom row: γ0 traces the lazy-to-rich axis within the mean-field family at λsp=1. PC-ALM at T=2L tracks BP across both axes; PC at T=2L tracks BP in the lazy regime but lags as the parameterization becomes rich.
Figure 7: MNIST counterpart of Figure 6. Same axes, same fixed (N,L) = (32, 64), same conclusion: PC-ALM tracks BP across the parameterization sweep; PC lags in the rich regime.

Figure 8: Two routes to BP-aligned hidden credit at L = 32, ReLU, Fashion-MNIST. Here T denotes the plotted per-sample update budget: activity steps for PC and joint primal-dual cycles for PC-ALM. Gray: PC at fixed inference budget T , sweeping hidden width N . Blue: PC-ALM (α = 1) at fixed N = 16, sweeping T . Orange star: BP reference at N = 16. The horizontal axis is per-step compute, proportional to TLN2. In this L = 32, ReLU/Fashion-MNIST setting, the PC-ALM branch reaches 0.9 cosine similarity to BP at roughly an order of magnitude less compute than the PC width sweeps shown.

Figure 9: MNIST counterpart of Figure 2. Same (N,L) grid, three seeds, α = 1. Same regime structure: PC-ALM at T = 2L tracks BP across the grid; PC drops in deep narrow networks; the gain concentrates in deep, narrow cells.
Figure 10: Training curves for one epoch at N = 32, L = 64 on Fashion-MNIST across identity / tanh / ReLU.
